newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on Akzo H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on Akzo H1 results.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel NV on Thursday reported first-half net profit rose by 100 million guilders to 799 million guilders and maintained its forecast that net profit for the full year would be higher than in 1996.
Below is a selection of analysts' comments:

"If you look at the operating result, pharmaceuticals and fibres are in line, coatings are on the upside and chemicals are a little bit up...This explains the higher result than expected...I had Akzo as a market performer and I don't see any reason to change that. Akzo may well have trouble into 1998 with higher prices for raw materials."

"It's really a very good performance. It was absolutely needed, given that the first quarter was a disappointment to the market. I was expecting (Q2 earnings per share) of 6.0 cents. This is far above consensus. The result at coatings was very strong. It's a major surprise to the market. They have stated they want to expand in coatings and pharmaceuticals. Pharmaceuticals was slightly better (than I expected), mainly due to currency factors. Chemicals was slightly disappointing. We had the stock as a short term buy. We are changing it to a strong buy."

"These results are even better than expected. They are excellent. Except in fibres, where textiles had not been expected to do so well, there are no negative elements. In spite of the 'pill' problems and the introduction costs of new drugs, the pharmaceuticals division managed to improve its margins to 20.3 percent in Q2 97 against 20.1 percent in the period a year ago, so underlying figures are even better. Coatings raised its margins to 11.8 from 9.9 percent a year ago, with turnover also on the increase -- the integration with Nobel has started structurally to bear fruit, and there's more to come.

"At the chemicals division, the lights are also on green, with margins pumped up to 9.3 from 7.8 percent in 2Q96. I will hike my earnings per share expectations, and we maintain our buy recommendation."
